facts.text: Myton’s name comes from a settler’s family, often said to be a shortened form of “My Town,” reflecting its close‑knit community spirit.
Before settlers arrived, the Ute people inhabited the area, living throughout the Uinta Basin for centuries.
The city sits on the south side of the Duchesne River, an east‑flowing tributary of the Green River.
Archaeologists in Myton have uncovered dinosaur fossils, including fossilized turtle eggs and full‑size skeletons, proving the basin once teemed with prehistoric giants.
In 1974, Myton recorded only 1.34 inches of rain, the lowest calendar‑year precipitation total ever in Utah and the second‑lowest in the U.S.
Myton’s history mirrors the broader Uinta Basin story of resilience, cooperation, and a deep connection to the land.
